title: Inanna/Ishtar, Goddess of the Sky
subject: Inanna-Ishtar, the sky and love goddess
description: A modern illustrative image of the Mesopotamian goddess Inanna (Sumerian) / Ishtar (Akkadian), the goddess of the sky, love, and war, associated with the star Venus.
alt: Inanna-Ishtar, the sky and love goddess — Inanna/Ishtar, Goddess of the Sky

title: The Ishtar Gate of Babylon
subject: The Ishtar Gate, dedicated to the goddess Ishtar
description: The reconstructed Ishtar Gate of Babylon (Neo-Babylonian, ca. 575 BCE), dedicated to the goddess Ishtar — glazed brickwork with processionalway reliefs of aurochs (mušḫušshu dragons) and lions.
alt: The Ishtar Gate, dedicated to the goddess Ishtar — The Ishtar Gate of Babylon

title: Hymn to the Goddess Ishtar (clay tablet)
subject: A hymn/ritual text of the goddess Ishtar
description: A Neo-Babylonian clay tablet preserving a hymn/ritual text of the goddess Ishtar from Babylon — a direct primary source for her worship.
alt: A hymn/ritual text of the goddess Ishtar — Hymn to the Goddess Ishtar (clay tablet)

title: Marduk's Battle with Tiamat (from the Enuma Elish)
subject: Marduk slaying Tiamat, the creation battle
description: A reconstructed scene of Marduk's battle with Tiamat from the Enuma Elish, the Babylonian creation epic in which Marduk defeats the primordial chaos-dragon.
alt: Marduk slaying Tiamat, the creation battle — Marduk's Battle with Tiamat (from the Enuma Elish)

title: Enuma Elish clay tablet (tablet IV)
subject: Tablet of the Enuma Elish, the Babylonian creation epic
description: A clay tablet of the Enuma Elish (British Museum), the Babylonian creation epic — among the oldest surviving copies of this central Mesopotamian myth.
alt: Tablet of the Enuma Elish, the Babylonian creation epic — Enuma Elish clay tablet (tablet IV)

title: The 'Queen of the Night' Relief (Burney Relief)
subject: A winged goddess — possibly Ishtar or the underworld queen Ereshkigal
description: The famous 'Queen of the Night' (Burney Relief) from Old Babylon: a winged, horned goddess on a throne. Identification is debated (Ishtar, Ereshkigal, or Lilith) — a prime example of the iconographic uncertainty in Mesopotamian religion.
alt: A winged goddess — possibly Ishtar or the underworld queen Ereshkigal — The 'Queen of the Night' Relief (Burney Relief)

title: Cylinder Seal of Shamash (Louvre AO 9132)
subject: The sun god Shamash in seal iconography
description: A Mesopotamian cylinder seal depicting the sun god Shamash (the god of justice and the 'light' that reveals truth) — cylinder seals are a major source for Mesopotamian divine iconography.
alt: The sun god Shamash in seal iconography — Cylinder Seal of Shamash (Louvre AO 9132)
